subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: A Toy manufacturer produces bicycles and tricycles, each of which must be processed through two machine A and B. Machine A has maximum of 120 hours available and machine B has a maximum of 180 hours available. Manufacturing a bicycle requires 4 hours on machine A and 10 hours on machine B. Manufacturing a tricycle required 6 hours on machine A and 3 hours on machine B. If profits are Rs.65 for a bicycle and Rs.45 for a tricycle, formulate L.P.P. to have maximum profit.
solution:
Let \(z\) be the profit, which can be made by manufacturing and selling \(x\) tricycles and \(y\) bicycles.

\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Total Profit \(z = 45x + 65y\), so Maximize \(z = 45x + 65y\).

The machine-hour requirements and availabilities are:

| Machine | Tricycles (x) | Bicycles (y) | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 6 | 4 | 120 |
| B | 3 | 10 | 180 |

From the table, the remaining conditions are \(6x + 4y \le 120\) and \(3x + 10y \le 180\).

The required formulated L.P.P. is as follows:

Maximize \(z = 45x + 65y\)

Subject to the constraints \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\), \(6x + 4y \le 120\), \(3x + 10y \le 180\).

subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: A company manufactures two types of toys A and B. Each toy of type A requires 2 minutes for cutting and 1 minute for assembling. Each toy of type B requires 3 minutes for cutting and 4 minutes for assembling. There are 3 hours available for cutting and 2 hours are available for assembling. On selling a toy of type A the company gets a profit of Rs.10 and that on toy of type B is Rs.20. Formulate the L.P.P. to maximize profit.
solution:
Suppose the company manufactures \(x\) toys of type A and \(y\) toys of type B.

\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Let \(P\) be the total profit. On selling a toy of type A, the company gets Rs.10 and that on a toy of type B is Rs.20.

Total profit on selling \(x\) toys of type A and \(y\) toys of type B is \(p = 10x + 20y\).

Maximize \(p = 10x + 20y\).

The conditions are \(2x + 3y \le 180\), \(x + 4y \le 120\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).

subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: A horticulturist wishes to mix two brands of fertilizers that will provide a minimum of 15 units of potash, 20 units of nitrate and 24 units of phosphate. One unit of brand I provides 3 units of potash, 1 unit of nitrate, 3 units of phosphate. One unit of brand II provides 1 unit of potash, 5 units of nitrate and 2 units of phosphates. One unit of brand I costs Rs.120 and one unit of brand II costs Rs.60 per unit. Formulate this problems as L.P.P. to minimize the cost.
solution:
Let \(z\) be the cost of the mixture prepared by mixing \(x\) units of brand I and \(y\) units of brand II. Then \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\).

Since 1 unit of brand I costs Rs.120 and 1 unit of brand II costs Rs.60, the total cost is \(z = 120x + 60y\), so Minimize \(z = 120x + 60y\).

The content per unit and minimum requirements are:

| Content | Brand I per unit | Brand II per unit | Minimum requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Potash | 3 | 1 | 15 |
| Nitrate | 1 | 5 | 20 |
| Phosphate | 3 | 2 | 24 |

The conditions are \(3x + y \ge 15\), \(x + 5y \ge 20\), \(3x + 2y \ge 24\).

The L.P.P. is: Minimize \(z = 120x + 60y\) subject to the above constraints, \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\).

subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem:
A manufacturing firm produces two types of gadgets A and B, which are first processed in the foundry and then sent to machine shop for finishing. The number of man hours of labour required in each shop for production of A and B per unit and the number of man hours available for the firm are as follows:

| Gadgets | Foundry | Machine Shop |
|---|---|---|
| A | 10 | 5 |
| B | 6 | 4 |
| Time available (hour) | 60 | 35 |

Profit on the sale of A is Rs. 30 and B is Rs. 20 per units. Formulate the L.P.P. to have maximum profit.

subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem:
In a cattle breading firm, it is prescribed that the food ration for one animal must contain 14, 22 and 1 units of nutrients A, B and C respectively. Two different kinds of fodder are available. Each unit of these two contains the following amounts of these three nutrients:

| Nutrient | Fodder 1 | Fodder 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Nutrients A | 2 | 1 |
| Nutrients B | 2 | 3 |
| Nutrients C | 1 | 1 |

The cost of fodder 1 is Rs.3 per unit and that of fodder Rs. 2. Formulate the L.P.P. to minimize the cost.

subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem:
A company manufactures two types of chemicals A and B. Each chemical requires two types of raw material P and Q. The table below shows number of units of P and Q required to manufacture one unit of A and one unit of B and the total availability of P and Q.

| Raw Material | A | B | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | 3 | 2 | 120 |
| Q | 2 | 5 | 160 |

The company gets profits of Rs.350 and Rs.400 by selling one unit of A and one unit of B respectively. (Assume that the entire production of A and B can be sold). How many units of the chemicals A and B should be manufactured so that the company get maximum profit? Formulate the problem as L.P.P. to maximize the profit.

subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: A printing company prints two types of magazines A and B. The company earns Rs. 10 and Rs. 15 on magazines A and B per copy. These are processed on three machines I, II, III. Magazine A requires 2 hours on Machine I, 5 hours on Machine II and 2 hours on Machine III. Magazine B requires 3 hours on Machine I, 2 hours on Machine II and 6 hours on Machine III. Machines I, II, III are available for 36, 50, 60 hours per week respectively. Formulate the L.P.P. to determine weekly production of A and B, so that the total profit is maximum.

subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: A manufacture produces bulbs and tubes. Each of these must be processed through two machines \(M_1\) and \(M_2\). A package of bulbs require 1 hour of work on Machine \(M_1\) and 3 hours of work on \(M_2\). A package of tubes require 2 hours on Machine \(M_1\) and 4 hours on Machine \(M_2\). He earns a profit of Rs. 13.5 per package of bulbs and Rs. 55 per package of tubes. Formulate the LLP to maximize the profit, if he operates the machine \(M_1\) for atmost 10 hours a day and machine \(M_2\) for atmost 12 hours a day.

subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem:
A company manufactures two types of fertilizers \(F_1\) and \(F_2\). Each type of fertilizer requires two raw materials A and B. The number of units of A and B required to manufacture one unit of fertilizer \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) and availability of the raw materials A and B per day are given in the table below:

| Raw Material | F1 | F2 | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 2 | 3 | 40 |
| B | 1 | 4 | 70 |

By selling one unit of \(F_1\) and one unit of \(F_2\), company gets a profit of Rs. 500 and Rs. 750 respectively. Formulate the problem as L.P.P. to maximize the profit.

subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: A doctor has prescribed two different units of foods A and B to form a weekly diet for a sick person. The minimum requirements of fats, carbohydrates and proteins are 18, 28, 14 units respectively. One unit of food A has 4 units of fats, 14 units of carbohydrates and 8 units of protein. One unit of food B has 6 units of fat, 12 units of carbohydrates and 8 units of protein. The price of food A is 4.5 per unit and that of food B is 3.5 per unit. Form the L.P.P. so that the sick person's diet meets the requirements at a minimum cost.

subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: If John drives a car at a speed of 60 kms/hour he has to spend Rs. 5 per km on petrol. If he drives at a faster speed of 90 kms/hour, the cost of petrol increases to 8 per km. He has Rs. 600 to spend on petrol and wishes to travel the maximum distance within an hour. Formulate the above problem as L.P.P.

subtopic: Formulation of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: The company makes concrete bricks made up of cement and sand. The weight of a concrete brick has to be least 5 kg. Cement costs Rs.20 per kg. and sand costs of Rs.6 per kg. strength consideration dictate that a concrete brick should contain minimum 4 kg. of cement and not more than 2 kg. of sand. Form the L.P.P. for the cost to be minimum.

subtopic: Graphical Solution of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: Solve graphically: Maximize \(z = 9x + 13y\) subject to \(2x + 3y \le 18\), \(2x + y \le 10\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).
solution:
To draw \(2x + 3y \le 18\) and \(2x + y \le 10\), draw lines \(2x + 3y = 18\) and \(2x + y = 10\).

| To draw | x | y | Line passes through | Sign | Region lies on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \(L_1: 2x + 3y = 18\) | 0 | 6 | \((0, 6)\) | \(\le\) | Origin side of \(L_1\) |
| \(L_1: 2x + 3y = 18\) | 9 | 0 | \((9, 0)\) | \(\le\) | Origin side of \(L_1\) |
| \(L_2: 2x + y = 10\) | 0 | 10 | \((0, 10)\) | \(\le\) | Origin side of \(L_2\) |
| \(L_2: 2x + y = 10\) | 5 | 0 | \((5, 0)\) | \(\le\) | Origin side of \(L_2\) |

The common shaded region \(OABCO\) is a feasible region with vertices \(O(0, 0)\), \(A(5, 0)\), \(B(3, 4)\), \(C(0, 6)\).

| Vertex \((x, y)\) | Value of \(z = 9x + 13y\) |
|---|---|
| \(O(0, 0)\) | 0 |
| \(A(5, 0)\) | 45 |
| \(B(3, 4)\) | 79 |
| \(C(0, 6)\) | 78 |

From the table, the maximum value of \(z = 79\) occurs at \(B(3, 4)\), i.e. when \(x = 3,\ y = 4\).

subtopic: Graphical Solution of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: Solve graphically: Maximize \(z = 5x + 2y\) subject to \(5x + y \ge 10\), \(x + y \ge 6\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).
solution:
To draw \(5x + y \ge 10\) and \(x + y \ge 6\), draw lines \(5x + y = 10\) and \(x + y = 6\).

| To draw | x | y | Line passes through | Sign | Region lies on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \(L_1: 5x + y = 10\) | 0 | 10 | \((0, 10)\) | \(\ge\) | Non-origin side of \(L_1\) |
| \(L_1: 5x + y = 10\) | 2 | 0 | \((2, 0)\) | \(\ge\) | Non-origin side of \(L_1\) |
| \(L_2: x + y = 6\) | 0 | 6 | \((0, 6)\) | \(\ge\) | Non-origin side of \(L_2\) |
| \(L_2: x + y = 6\) | 6 | 0 | \((6, 0)\) | \(\ge\) | Non-origin side of \(L_2\) |

The common shaded region is the feasible region with vertices \(A(6, 0)\), \(B(1, 5)\), \(C(0, 10)\).

| Vertex \((x, y)\) | Value of \(z = 5x + 2y\) |
|---|---|
| \(A(6, 0)\) | 30 |
| \(B(1, 5)\) | 15 |
| \(C(0, 10)\) | 20 |

From the table, the maximum value of \(z = 15\) occurs at \(B(1, 5)\), i.e. when \(x = 1,\ y = 5\). [Note: the textbook prints the objective as 'Maximize' but the feasible region is unbounded above and the book reports the value 15 at \(B(1,5)\), which is actually the minimum among the listed vertices — a book defect; the printed conclusion is preserved verbatim.]

subtopic: Graphical Solution of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: Solve graphically: Maximize \(z = 3x + 4y\) subject to \(x - y \ge 0\), \(-x + 3y \le 3\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).
solution:
To draw \(x - y \ge 0\) and \(-x + 3y \le 3\), draw lines \(x - y = 0\) (i.e. \(x = y\)) and \(-x + 3y = 3\).

| To draw | Draw line | x | y | Line passes through | Sign | Region lies on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \(x - y \ge 0\) | \(L_1: x = y\) | 0 | 0 | \((0, 0)\) | \(\ge\) | A side |
| \(x - y \ge 0\) | \(L_1: x = y\) | 1 | 1 | \((1, 1)\) | \(\ge\) | A side |
| \(-x + 3y \le 3\) | \(L_2: -x + 3y = 3\) | 0 | 1 | \((0, 1)\) | \(\le\) | Origin side of \(L_2\) |
| \(-x + 3y \le 3\) | \(L_2: -x + 3y = 3\) | -3 | 0 | \((-3, 0)\) | \(\le\) | Origin side of \(L_2\) |

From the graph, the common shaded area is the feasible region which is unbounded (not a polygon). In such cases the iso-profit lines can be moved away from the origin indefinitely. Hence there is no finite maximum value of \(z\) within the feasible region.

subtopic: Graphical Solution of a Linear Programming Problem
stem: Solve graphically: Maximize \(z = 5x + 2y\) subject to \(3x + 5y \le 15\), \(5x + 2y \le 10\), \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\).
solution:
To draw \(3x + 5y \le 15\) and \(5x + 2y \le 10\), draw lines \(3x + 5y = 15\) and \(5x + 2y = 10\).

| To draw | x | y | Line passes through | Sign | Region lies on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \(L_1: 3x + 5y = 15\) | 5 | 0 | \((5, 0)\) | \(\le\) | Origin side of \(L_1\) |
| \(L_1: 3x + 5y = 15\) | 0 | 3 | \((0, 3)\) | \(\le\) | Origin side of \(L_1\) |
| \(L_2: 5x + 2y = 10\) | 2 | 0 | \((2, 0)\) | \(\le\) | Origin side of \(L_2\) |
| \(L_2: 5x + 2y = 10\) | 0 | 5 | \((0, 5)\) | \(\le\) | Origin side of \(L_2\) |

The shaded region \(OABC\) is the feasible region with the vertices \(O(0, 0)\), \(A(2, 0)\), \(B\left(\dfrac{20}{19}, \dfrac{45}{19}\right)\), \(C(0, 3)\).

\(Z_O = 0\), \(Z_A = 10\), \(Z_B = 10\), \(Z_C = 6\).

The maximum value of \(z\) occurs at \(A\) and \(B\) and is \(z = 10\). The maximum value of \(z\) occurs at every point lying on the segment \(AB\). Hence there are infinite number of optimal solutions.
